subject: Performance SLO - Private/VPC network qualification
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acmecloud.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-25T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs & Private/VPC network qualification

Hi Tom + Priya - great to meet today, thanks for the detailed run-through. Recap and next steps below from our side (open to edits):

Summary of perf targets you confirmed during the call:
- P95 latency target (in-region): 30-50 ms for single-turn text generation (non-streamed).
- Streaming responses: support token/edge streaming with p95 <= 60 ms to the client for initial chunks (we'll clarify chunk sizes below).
- Throughput/concurrency: expected sustained throughput of ~200 requests/sec with concurrency up to ~50 simultaneous connections for the service fronting the model.
- Burst capacity: occasional spikes to ~500 req/s (10-15s) expected during deploy windows.

Private/VPC-specific items we need to qualify:
1) Network path and peering: you mentioned Direct Connect to us-west-2 - can you confirm whether traffic to Redwood's VPC will be via AWS Direct Connect + Private VIF or over IPSec VPN? If Direct Connect, what's the advertised bandwidth and any cross-connect limits?
2) Egress/firewall rules: please send the specific IP ranges and ports your firewall team will allow for outbound rules to Redwood. We'll provide the minimal set for control plane and data plane.
3) Latency budget inside Acme: what are your internal network latencies from application frontends to your egress/NAT (expected median and p95)?
4) Packet captures/network tests: please run a 5-10 minute packet capture from an application node to your egress and share a pcap (we listed a short test plan in requested_network_tests.md attached).
5) VPN/Peering configuration: if you use IPSec, can you share the tunnel config and any MTU adjustments (we have known issues when DF causes fragmentation on UDP/gRPC).

Attachments included: slo_requirements.xlsx (SLO matrix), requested_network_tests.md (quick test plan).

Next steps / owners:
- Acme (Tom/Priya): confirm Direct Connect vs VPN, share topology + preliminary packet capture - target: 3/27 EOD PT.
- Redwood (Marissa/Jordan): we'll produce a minimal egress IP list and a small synthetic test harness to run once we have the topology - target: 3/28.
- Tech sync: propose 30-min follow-up after you share the pcap, Jordan will lead the packet review.

If that looks right I'll follow up with the minimal egress IPs and an invite for the sync.

Thanks
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0184

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs & Private/VPC network qualification

Thanks Marissa - good summary. Quick answers from our side:
- We have AWS Direct Connect with a Private VIF into our us-west-2 account (10 Gbps advertised). Traffic to vendor VPCs today generally flows over DX + VPC peering or Transit Gateway depending on the partner. We can set up a Private VIF to Redwood if needed.
- Attached: network_topology.pdf (diagram) and acme_vpn_config.txt (current IPSec tunnel config for one partner).
- Internal latency: from frontend app to our egress (NAT/edge) median is ~7 ms, p95 ~18 ms in healthy zones.
- Regarding streaming: we can support chunked streaming; our apps typically expect the first token/chunk within 100 ms, so your 60 ms p95 would be helpful.

We'll pull a packet capture during our 3/27 maintenance window (02:00-03:00 PT) from an app node to the egress and upload the pcap.

Questions for Redwood:
- For streaming, do you recommend server-side SSE/chunked HTTP, or gRPC trailers for lower overhead? Any preference for MTU tuning?
- Do you require a static source IP for egress to map firewall rules?

Best,
Tom

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acmecloud.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-26T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs & Private/VPC network qualification

Tom - thanks, this is very helpful. A few clarifications and suggestions from our infra team (copied):

1) Streaming protocol: we support both chunked HTTP (server-sent events / chunked Transfer-Encoding) and gRPC streaming. For lowest tail latency we generally recommend gRPC over HTTP/2 for internal private connections - it avoids some buffering by LB/proxies. If your stack uses HTTP/1.1 and you need SSE we can make that work but may see slightly higher p95.

2) MTU and fragmentation: please keep MTU >= 1400 on the tunnel to avoid fragmentation for our UDP-based inference kernels. If you see PMTU blackhole symptoms, reducing to 1400 usually resolves it.

3) Static egress IPs: we can provide a small set of static IPs for data-plane egress to simplify firewall rules. For private deployments these are typically the VPC NAT IPs or a transit IP range - we'll give the list in the follow-up.

4) Tests & packet capture: perfect to capture during your 3/27 window. When you upload the pcap please include: source app node IP, timestamp range, and which test scenario (steady 200 rps / spike test). Jordan will review the pcap and confirm whether we see any retransmits/large RTT variance.

5) Synthetic harness: Dev will send a small harness (curl/gRPC client + small dataset) you can run from an app node to validate p95 under target throughput. Dev: can you attach the harness and a short runbook to the Drive link?

I've attached a quick SLO matrix in slo_requirements.xlsx - it maps our recommended SLOs to what we discussed. If that works, I'll schedule the 30-min packet-review sync for 3/28 10:00 PT.

Thanks
Marissa
